title: The Barrow Wight
text: A wight sits cross-legged on a burial mound, thin as winter, its eyes two cold sparks. Around it on the grass lie shadows without bodies, pinned down like pelts to dry. It asks riddles, it says, and if you answer wrong it keeps your shadow.

outcomes.text: Right, every one. It hisses, and gives up a grave-good from the mound.
Wrong. It reaches out and peels their shadow off the grass like a skin.

options.label: The shrewdest answers with a riddle of their own.

outcomes.text: It is still thinking when you leave, cold eyes narrowed, muttering.
It unfolds from the mound, long and thin, and the shadows on the grass begin to move.
